question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer is configuring a VSAN on the network. Which option must be selected to create the VSAN?
context: UCS Manager GUI: Create VSAN dialog with options Common/Global, Fabric A, Fabric B, Both Fabrics Configured Differently; and FC Zoning Settings checkbox 'FC Zoning Enabled'. Network topology shows Fabric A dedicated to the new SAN VSAN.
imageNote: Diagram: Storage connects via VLAN2001/VLAN2002 clouds and NPIV to N5K-A and N5K-B switches, which connect down to FI-A and FI-B, which both connect to the Cisco UCS Chassis.
theory: VSANs on a Cisco UCS fabric interconnect can be scoped as Common/Global (present identically on both fabrics), pinned to one specific fabric (A or B), or configured differently per fabric. When the SAN topology dedicates Fabric A entirely to the new VSAN's traffic (with no equivalent presence needed on Fabric B), the VSAN must be created scoped to Fabric A specifically, rather than Common/Global (which would also place it on Fabric B) or Fabric B (the wrong side entirely). (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Storage Management, VSAN Configuration)
